### CVE-2025-26465 — Openssh: machine-in-the-middle attack if verifyhostkeydns is enabled
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2025-02-18 | Updated: 2026-11-24 | Max CVSS: 6.8
- CWE: CWE-390 Detection of Error Condition Without Action
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 6.8 MEDIUM `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- CVSS 3.1 (nvd:secalert@redhat.com:Secondary): 6.8 MEDIUM `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- CVSS 3.1 (nvd:nvd@nist.gov:Primary): 6.8 MEDIUM `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`

A vulnerability was found in OpenSSH when the VerifyHostKeyDNS option is enabled. A machine-in-the-middle attack can be performed by a malicious machine impersonating a legit server. This issue occurs due to how OpenSSH mishandles error codes in specific conditions when verifying the host key. For an attack to be considered successful, the attacker needs to manage to exhaust the client's memory resource first, turning the attack complexity high.

**workarounds:** This issue can be mitigated by disabling VerifyHostKeyDNS by setting that option to 'no' in an SSH client configuration file (such as /etc/ssh/ssh_config, ~/.ssh/config, or one of the files in the /etc/ssh/ssh_config.d/ directory). This is the default configuration in Red Hat Enterprise Linux.

For configurations that require VerifyHostKeyDNS to be enabled (set to either 'yes' or 'ask'), mitigation for this issue is either not available or the currently available options do not meet the Red Hat Product Security criteria comprising ease of use and deployment, applicability to widespread installation base or stability.

### CVE-2025-26466 — Openssh: denial-of-service in openssh
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2025-02-28 | Updated: 2026-11-24 | Max CVSS: 5.9
- CWE: CWE-770 Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 5.9 MEDIUM `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial
- CVSS 3.1 (nvd:secalert@redhat.com:Secondary): 5.9 MEDIUM `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- CVSS 3.1 (nvd:nvd@nist.gov:Primary): 5.9 MEDIUM `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`

A flaw was found in the OpenSSH package. For each ping packet the SSH server receives, a pong packet is allocated in a memory buffer and stored in a queue of packages. It is only freed when the server/client key exchange has finished. A malicious client may keep sending such packages, leading to an uncontrolled increase in memory consumption on the server side. Consequently, the server may become unavailable, resulting in a denial of service attack.

**workarounds:** This issue can be mitigated by setting the following three different options in the sshd configuration file located at: /etc/ssh/sshd_config

MaxStartups: Set to a reasonable value, this option controls the maximum number of concurrent unauthenticated connections the SSH server accepts;

PerSourcePenalties: Set its suboptions to a reasonable value, this option is used to help sshd to detect and drop connections that are potentially malicious for the SSH server;

LoginGraceTime: Set to a resonable value, this option controls how much time the SSH server will wait the client to authenticate before dropping its connection;

All the three option above needs to be set to implement a full mitigation for this vulnerability.

### CVE-2025-61984
- Assigner: mitre | Published: 2025-10-06 | Updated: 2026-11-10 | Max CVSS: 3.6
- CWE: CWE-159 CWE-159 Improper Handling of Invalid Use of Special Elements
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 3.6 LOW `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

ssh in OpenSSH before 10.1 allows control characters in usernames that originate from certain possibly untrusted sources, potentially leading to code execution when a ProxyCommand is used. The untrusted sources are the command line and %-sequence expansion of a configuration file. (A configuration file that provides a complete literal username is not categorized as an untrusted source.)

- OpenBSD / OpenSSH: affected 0 <10.1 (custom)
